corrections.why: The tower is Little Snowball Lookout, atop Little Snowball Mountain, and the state list's shorter name may refer to it. A human should confirm the match before the record name changes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR credits volunteers with dismantling it in the 1980s; Get Up and Go Camping and the Big Ivy blog credit Lloyd Allen, and place the removal in 1980 or around 1985.
Re-erection in 2006 (Get Up and Go Camping) and dedication in 2007 (Big Ivy blog) are probably both correct, since the blog describes a year of volunteer work after the move.
The NHLR says the Big Ivy Historical Society Center is near Bernardsville; Get Up and Go Camping and the Big Ivy blog say Barnardsville, where the park is. Treated as a spelling error in the NHLR.

Get Up and Go Camping says the pieces sat in storage for more than a quarter century; the Big Ivy blog says they were stored for twenty years after Allen removed the tower around 1985. The story attributes each figure to its source and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The record name 'Snowball Mtn' comes from the TN Landforms list, and the story assumes that entry is Little Snowball Lookout; that link is inferred, not stated by a source. The record coordinates (35.72583, -82.42666) were not checked against the original site or the Big Ivy park, so check them before using them on the map. The 6.4 m height is the 21-foot steel frame converted to metres; no source gives the cab floor height separately. Mote Allen's years of service are not given. The story says nothing about fires, and access at Big Ivy Historical Park is not described in any source read, so no access level is set. Two of the four sources are blogs; the NHLR is the only register entry.
